findings.F1: The Calmar fails (0.577 = a 30.6% yearly return over a 53.0% deepest fall) because of one 413-day fall across w2–w5 (2022), during which the coins' summed daily moves were +0.77 while the book was short on 54% of days with a mean position of only 0.04; the next falls, -44.2% (w19–w20) and -43.4% (w16–17), also had the book short on about half their days (48% and 60%).
findings.F2: The short side carries almost none of the book's gain: short coin-days earn a mean of 0.000189 per day (n=2866) against 0.001857 for long coin-days (n=2793), with similar spread (std 0.0245 against 0.0270).
findings.F3: Shorts held while the coin's 30-day return is in its highest third lose 0.0011 per day (n=182) and earn 0.0011 per day in its lowest third (n=1242); longs earn 0.0024 per day in the highest third (n=1251) against 0.0011 in the lowest (n=180), so the book pays when the RSI side and the 30-day move agree.
findings.F4: Shorts held in the highest third of the coin's 30-day realised volatility lose 0.00028 per day (n=866) and earn 0.00097 in the lowest third (n=622); longs earn 0.00295 per day in the lowest-volatility third (n=799) against 0.00092 in the highest (n=549), so the signal pays most in calm markets.
findings.F5: Shorts held after the highest third of the 7-day return lose 0.00115 per day (n=780) and earn 0.00053 after the lowest third (n=992).
findings.F6: The short side lost in five of eight years, worst in 2020 (-0.00375 per day, n=205); it gained only in the falling years 2018, 2022 and 2025, while the long side lost only in 2018 and 2022 (-0.00237 per day, n=131).

ideas.idea: The larger the share of the past 30 days that a coin's 14-day RSI has spent below its midpoint of 50, the lower the coin's return over the next 14 days, and the more so the further the coin's own 30-day return lies on the same side as that RSI share (falling for a large share below, rising for a small one).
ideas.consequence: Size a short on RSI time-below-50 up only as the coin's 30-day price move confirms the decline, and size it down when the coin has been rising; this cuts the shorts held into rallies that dug the deepest falls.
ideas.name: RSI share confirmed by trend

ideas.idea: The larger the share of the past 30 days that a coin's 14-day RSI has spent below its midpoint of 50, the lower the coin's return over the next 14 days, and the more so the lower the coin's 30-day realised volatility.
ideas.consequence: Lean harder on the RSI-share signal in calm markets and less in turbulent ones, where its short side has lost money.
ideas.name: RSI share in calm markets
